assessments.task: Use the whole-body envelope to point to the shoulder, hand and foot outlines from the anterior view, then confirm their depth in the oblique view.

axes.observation: The export names the BodyParts3D FJ2810 source and retains its documented frame. A direct comparison to the source member is missing for the hand and foot landmarks.
The posterior silhouette and both Body Systems views show distinct fingers and foot contours. The retained plates lack a neutral close-up that can explain the detail around the digits and foot edges.

In the anterior plate I could identify the shoulder, hand and foot contours. The oblique plate shows the shoulder depth and distinguishes the palm from the chest. The posterior view distinguishes the two hands and both foot outlines. The skeleton plate supplies orientation, with the same-source skeleton outside the envelope export.

The 4,901,132-byte shell contains 203,382 triangles in one primitive, with no separate teaching selections. At the 680-pixel Body Systems plate width, 75.2% of front-facing triangles project below one square pixel anteriorly and 78.7% obliquely. This counts projected faces before occlusion. The finger and foot silhouettes still need protection in any lighter trial.
